section_summary.extract_value: This discussion summarizes findings from a single study examining relationships between multiple MAIA subscales and five facets of body image in a community sample of adult men and women. MAIA subscales accounted for substantial variance in body appreciation (44.0%), functionality appreciation (29.6%), and body pride (23.0%), with Trusting and regulatory subscales emerging as important predictors, while BMI, age, and sex were included as demographic covariates. The section notes limitations (self-report measures, poor internal consistency for some MAIA subscales, lack of objective interoceptive measures) and recommends targeted interventions and future research.
